blocks.prompt: 5 Prove that \(f(x) = \frac{\ln(2x)}{x^{2}}\) has local maximum at \(x = \frac{\sqrt{e}}{2}\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh "prove that" wala sawal hai: point humein diya hua hai, sirf saabit karna hai ke wahan local maximum hai.
Diya: \(f(x) = \frac{\ln(2x)}{x^{2}}\); \(\ln\) ki wajah se sirf \(x > 0\) par defined.
Rule: Second Derivative Test: \(f'(c) = 0\) aur \(f''(c) < 0\) to relative maximum.
Plan: quotient rule se \(f'\), dikhana ke diye gaye point par \(f' = 0\), phir \(f''\) ka sign negative dikhana.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(x) = \frac{\ln(2x)}{x^{2}}\), \(x > 0\).
Saabit karna: \(x = \frac{\sqrt{e}}{2}\) par local maximum hai.
Tareeqa: Second Derivative Test, do sharten dikhani hain: \(f'(c) = 0\) aur \(f''(c) < 0\).

Pehla derivative
\[f'(x) = \dfrac{x^{2} \cdot \frac{1}{x} - \ln(2x) \cdot 2x}{x^{4}}\]
\[= \dfrac{x - 2x\ln(2x)}{x^{4}}\]
\[= \dfrac{1 - 2\ln(2x)}{x^{3}}\]
Kyun: quotient rule: (neeche wala \(\times\) upar wale ka derivative \(-\) upar wala \(\times\) neeche wale ka derivative) \(\div\) neeche wale ka square. \(\frac{d}{dx}\ln(2x) = \frac{1}{2x} \cdot 2 = \frac{1}{x}\). Aakhir mein upar neeche se ek \(x\) cancel kiya.
Dhyan dein: \(\ln(2x)\) ka derivative \(\frac{1}{x}\) hai, \(\frac{1}{2x}\) nahin; chain rule ka 2 cancel kar deta hai.

Stationary point
\[1 - 2\ln(2x) = 0\]
\[\ln(2x) = \tfrac{1}{2} \Rightarrow 2x = e^{1/2}\]
\[x = \dfrac{\sqrt{e}}{2}\]
Kyun: \(x > 0\) ke liye \(x^{3} > 0\), is liye sirf numerator zero ho sakta hai. \(\ln u = k\) ka matlab \(u = e^{k}\). Yani diya gaya point waqai stationary hai: pehli shart poori.

Doosra derivative
\(f'(x) = \frac{u}{v}\) likhein, jahan \(u = 1 - 2\ln(2x)\) aur \(v = x^{3}\):
\[f''(x) = \dfrac{u'v - uv'}{v^{2}}\]
\[u' = -\dfrac{2}{x}\]
Kyun: dobara quotient rule. Chalaaki yeh hai ke \(x = \frac{\sqrt{e}}{2}\) par \(u = 0\) hai, is liye \(uv'\) wali term khud zero ho jati hai; poora \(f''\) simplify karne ki zaroorat nahin.

Point par \(f''\) ki value
\[f''\left(\tfrac{\sqrt{e}}{2}\right) = \dfrac{u'}{v} = -\dfrac{2}{x^{4}}\]
\[x^{4} = \dfrac{e^{2}}{16}\]
\[f''\left(\tfrac{\sqrt{e}}{2}\right) = -\dfrac{32}{e^{2}} < 0\]
Kyun: \(\frac{u'v}{v^{2}} = \frac{u'}{v} = \frac{-2/x}{x^{3}} = -\frac{2}{x^{4}}\); aur \(\left(\frac{\sqrt{e}}{2}\right)^{4} = \frac{e^{2}}{16}\), to \(-2 \times \frac{16}{e^{2}} = -\frac{32}{e^{2}}\). Doosri shart bhi poori.

Natija
\(f'\left(\frac{\sqrt{e}}{2}\right) = 0\) aur \(f''\left(\frac{\sqrt{e}}{2}\right) < 0\), is liye \(x = \frac{\sqrt{e}}{2}\) par local maximum hai.
\[f\left(\tfrac{\sqrt{e}}{2}\right) = \dfrac{\ln\sqrt{e}}{e/4} = \dfrac{1/2}{e/4} = \dfrac{2}{e}\]
Kyun: Second Derivative Test. Value sawal mein nahin maangi, lekin likh dena achha hai: \(\ln\sqrt{e} = \frac{1}{2}\).

Tasdeeq: \(\frac{\sqrt{e}}{2} \approx 0.824\). \(x = 0.7\) par \(\ln 1.4 \approx 0.34 < 0.5\), to \(f' > 0\); \(x = 1\) par \(\ln 2 \approx 0.69 > 0.5\), to \(f' < 0\). Sign plus se minus hua: first derivative bhi maximum hi batata hai.
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(f'\left(\frac{\sqrt{e}}{2}\right) = 0\) aur \(f''\left(\frac{\sqrt{e}}{2}\right) = -\frac{32}{e^{2}} < 0\), is liye \(x = \frac{\sqrt{e}}{2}\) par \(f\) ka local maximum hai (maximum value \(\frac{2}{e}\)).
